_comment: Canned model replies for verify-worker.sh. The mock endpoint reads the
'TARGET FILE: <path>' line out of the prompt worker.py sent, so the key is the
file being asked about; '<path>#<n>' answers the n-th call for that path
(rejection feedback and acceptance retries both count), and '*' is the
fallback. A string value is served as the assistant's raw content; an object
value is served as its JSON encoding, which is how the well-formed replies
stay readable here. The literal '__http500__' makes the endpoint fail instead.
No live model is involved in any of this, and no reply here is application
code for any real project - they are the smallest files that make the

good._why: The happy path: one valid reply per declared file. 'contents' is a string here and a list of lines for the test file, so both accepted shapes are exercised.

wrong-path._why: Every reply answers about a file the ticket did not declare. The script must refuse it, not write it, and stop with the model-unusable code.

extra-files-key._why: A reply that is right about the target file AND smuggles a second file alongside it. Rejected; the retry is clean, so the run finishes and src/sneaky.py must not exist anywhere.

extra_files.src/sneaky.py: print('this file was never declared by any ticket')

readme-target._why: The model tries to answer about the target README. Refused on the path check every time; the README must be byte-identical afterwards.

needs-file._why: The sanctioned way to say the ticket is under-specified. Must comment, write nothing, and exit with its own code.

src/slug.py.reason: the package needs an explicit __init__.py before src.slug imports

retry-then-pass._why: First implementation fails the acceptance command; the failure is fed back and the second attempt passes. Proves the retry is real and that it converges.

retry-exhausted._why: The implementation never passes. The worker must exhaust its attempts and commit NOTHING - the failure mode that matters most, because committing anyway would look like success.

prose._why: Never returns JSON at all - the failure the planner met on four live runs. The retry loop must exhaust and the script must stop loudly with the raw reply.
prose.*:
Sure! Here is how I would implement it:

1. Create the module
2. Add a test

Would you like me to continue?

http-500._why: The endpoint is down. A transport failure has no reply to feed back, so it is retried with a backoff and then reported as the model being unusable.

suite-breaks._why: Issue #39. The ticket's own acceptance command passes while a test the worker did not write starts failing. Report it, commit nothing, and never touch the test.

weakens-test._why: Issue #40. First reply deletes an existing test, second one switches it off with a skip marker. Both refused; the file on the branch must be untouched.

weakens-then-fixes._why: Issue #40 again: the same deletion, then a reply that keeps every existing test and adds the new one. The positive control for the weakening check - it must be a rejection that can be recovered from, not a dead end.

runtime-scope._why: Issue #41. Both declared files are written correctly and the acceptance command passes, but importing the module creates cache.db, which no ticket declared. Only a git-level scope gate catches this - inspecting the replies cannot.

dependency-bad._why: Issue #44. The manifest reply adds a package the target README does not sanction. ORCHESTRATOR.md: no dependency outside the README's '## Implementation constraints' list - and the worker's container reaches a registry, so an unsanctioned package would actually be installed and run.

dependency-ok._why: Issue #44 again, with only what the README's '## Implementation constraints' section sanctions. The positive control for the check above: it must permit a legitimate manifest, or it would block the work it is meant to police.

dependency-substring._why: Issue #44 a third time. Every package here is a real PyPI distribution whose name is a SUBSTRING of the fixture README's prose - 'api' in "no API here", 'requests' in "nothing requests anything", 're' in "re-exported". None is on the sanctioned list. The check used to be a substring search over the whole README and would have permitted all three; this scenario is the regression test that it is now an exact match against one named section.

no-change._why: Issue #40 with a reply that is byte-identical to what is already on the default branch. Nothing to commit is its own outcome: an empty pull request would read as success.
